content.text:
I replaced all 7 `datetime.utcnow()` calls with `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` and added `timezone` to the `datetime` import in each of the five files. All 5 tests pass, and I ran them with DeprecationWarnings treated as errors. A search finds no `utcnow` or `utcfromtimestamp` left.

Files changed: `app/audit.py`, `app/billing.py`, `app/cache.py` (2 calls), `app/reports.py` (2 calls), `app/sessions.py`.

One visible change: `reports.header()` now prints an offset at the end of the time, e.g. `T generated 2026-10-20T01:14:00+00:00` instead of `...01:14:00`. That's because `isoformat()` includes the offset when the time has a timezone. The test only checks the prefix, so it still passes. Anything that reads that exact string elsewhere would need to expect the offset.

`generated_at()`, `stamp()`, `due_date()`, `new_session()` and `cache.Entry` now hold timezone-aware times. Comparing one of these with an old timezone-naive time raises `TypeError`, so any stored or external naive times that get compared with them would have to be converted first. Nothing in this repo does that.
